quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [The Night Market Returns] After a three-year break, the Dockside Night Market reopens this Friday with more than sixty stalls. Visitors will find the usual street food, but organizers have added a section for local makers selling ceramics, jewelry, and printed fabric. The market will run every Friday and Saturday from 5 p.m. until midnight through September. Entry is free, although the nearby car park charges a flat $6 after 6 p.m. Surveys from before the break suggested that most visitors came for the atmosphere rather than for shopping, so live music has been scheduled at the north end.

Parking near the market has become expensive.
Local makers are struggling to sell their work.
Visitors prefer shopping to street food.
quests.correctAnswer: A popular market is reopening with some new features.
quests.hint: Ask which idea covers most of the details rather than just one of them.
quests.explanation: The passage announces that the market reopens and then lists what is new and how it will run. Parking is only one small detail.
quests.evidenceLine: reopens this Friday with more than sixty stalls

quests.passage: [The Watch] When my grandfather died, the only thing I asked for was his watch, which hadn't worked for decades. The writer decided to leave it broken.
The writer went to a third repairer.
The writer received a phone call.

quests.explanation: The second repairer's price was too high, and the next event is the visit to the third repairer, who agreed to try.
quests.evidenceLine: It was the third, a woman working above a shoe shop

quests.passage: [Understanding Minimum Payments] Each month, a credit card statement shows a "minimum payment", the smallest amount you must pay to avoid a late fee. quests.explanation: The passage says paying even slightly more than the minimum shortens the time you are in debt.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Apps or Classes?] Language apps and classroom courses suit different learners. An app lets you practice for ten minutes on a bus, costs little, and rewards you with streaks that make it easy to stay motivated. Its weakness is speaking: apps rarely correct pronunciation or let you hold a real conversation. A class offers that interaction and a teacher who notices your particular mistakes, but it demands a fixed schedule and a bigger budget. Many learners therefore combine the two, using an app for daily vocabulary and a weekly class for conversation.
quests.question: Which statement best compares the two options?
options: Apps give learners more speaking practice, but classes cost less.
Classes are cheaper and more flexible than apps, but less social.
Apps and classes are equally good at correcting a learner's mistakes.
Apps are cheaper and more flexible, but classes offer more interaction.
quests.correctAnswer: Apps are cheaper and more flexible, but classes offer more interaction.
quests.hint: Match each strength and weakness to the right option.
quests.explanation: Apps are low-cost and easy to fit in, while classes provide conversation and feedback but need a schedule and budget.
quests.evidenceLine: A class offers that interaction and a teacher who notices your particular mistakes

The writer thinks the recipe is too complicated.
The writer wants to try something new.

quests.hint: Consider why the writer says it after looking at the sister.
quests.explanation: Calling a choice "bold" in this way is a polite joke: the writer doubts cinnamon suits the soup and the pair choose cumin.

Tilly: I'll keep the garage door shut from now on. Mr. Kerr: Much appreciated. I do enjoy a quiet Sunday afternoon.
quests.question: Why does Tilly agree to keep the garage door shut?
options: She is planning to move house next month.
She dislikes the song the band keeps playing.
She understands that the neighbor is bothered.
She has finished practicing for the gig.
quests.correctAnswer: She understands that the neighbor is bothered.
quests.hint: Think about what Tilly has understood from Mr. Kerr's comments.
quests.explanation: Tilly responds to his hints by offering to keep the door shut, which shows she realized the noise was a problem.
quests.evidenceLine: I'll keep the garage door shut from now on
